Dyson photo matching results

Gemini correctly resolved 37 of 57 single-model photographs. Five answers were confidently wrong and 15 were not sure.

64.9%Correct overall
5Confidently wrong
15Not sure
₹5.21Per photo, revised Gemini run

Whole-photo scoring and the revised pipeline

ApproachCorrectConfidently wrongNot sureCost/photo
Whole photo, one reference; Qwen 3.7 Flash, threshold 9023/57125₹0.05
Object grouping and manufacturer evidence; Gemini 3.7 Flash high37/57515₹5.21

The baseline reproduces the client's scoring method with Qwen after the Gemini Argon baseline was stopped for cost. This comparison changes both the model and the method. The Gemini run correctly matched 28 catalogue photos and rejected nine outside-catalogue photos. It also returned the correct V12/V15 set in the separate two-model photograph.

The revised run cost is divided by all 58 photographs. It excludes earlier shared detection and embedding work; including that work is about ₹5.36/photo. These are public development photographs with source-derived labels. Client-store holdout accuracy has not been measured.

Models on the same 15 photographs

ModelCorrectConfidently wrongNot sureCost/photo
Gemini 3.7 Flash high11/1513₹1.38
GPT-6.1 Sol high6/1518₹3.21
Agreement between both6/1509₹4.43
Qwen 3.8 Max2/15013₹5.20

Requiring agreement removed the wrong answer in this small comparison, while leaving nine photographs unresolved. On these same 15 photos, the later Gemini workflow returned 10 correct, two confidently wrong and three not sure, regressing from the earlier 11 correct, one wrong and three not sure. Gemini, Sol and their agreement returned the correct model set in the additional two-model photograph. Costs include shared pipeline work and retained failed-call reserves where recorded.

In the earlier paired Qwen 3.7 Flash test, adding telling-details cards changed nine correct, four confidently wrong and two not sure to eight correct, two confidently wrong and five not sure. The cards reduced wrong confident answers while increasing unresolved photos; this is not evidence of a universal accuracy gain.

What the recovery rounds changed

Comparing aligned manufacturer views recovered six of the original 20 failures, introduced one confidently wrong answer and left 13 not sure. Two of three previously correct controls stayed correct; one became not sure. This was a selected-failure experiment, not a fresh full-set score. Its cost was about ₹8.40 per selected photo, including the separate control retry.

OpenRouter's Mistral OCR checked P054 and the 13 remaining unsure photos. It found no usable model or part identifiers and recovered no identities. Reported cost was ₹0.19/photo; an additional parser-fee reserve remains in the spending ledger.

P054 remains a recorded failure: the source identifies Gen5detect, while the aligned-reference round returned V16 at 95. The shared controls, screen and filter were insufficient to distinguish them. The app therefore shows supporting and missing details beside its qualitative confidence. That confidence is a model assessment, not a measured probability.
